originality.rationale: The full eligible primary source and closest open 2023 full text discuss one biased additive root and a two-point outward-escaping multiplicative oracle, not the sharp three-atom balanced-inward classification and positive-probability convergence to one of two false attractors. Ten published-finding corpus searches returned related but non-implicating records. This conclusion is best-knowledge, with acknowledged unindexed/history risks.

value.rationale: A mathematically natural sign-balanced multiplicative stochastic oracle can have multiple false attracting equilibria only after exactly three distinct sampled curvature atoms, with an explicit sharp sign and probability threshold. The actual Robbins–Monro clipped process has a rigorously positive chance of converging to a wrong attractor whereas its unclipped counterpart converges to the true strongly convex optimum; this isolates clipping-specific failure inside a bounded, globally inward mean-field regime.
